data.narrative:
Helion Energy, a Series G nuclear energy company founded by David Kirtley and Chris Pihl, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 nuclear technology peers—3 public and 8 private—spanning similar valuation tiers. The company has raised over $1.5B to date against a current post-money valuation of $15.5B.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression analysis applies a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier to Helion's last post-money valuation of $5.4B, implying a value of $6.8B at the next funding stage. Peer-Median analysis across three same-sector comparables—Oklo (public, $7.0B), Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), and X-Energy (public, $5.6B)—yields a median valuation of $6.0B, with a range of $5.6B to $7.0B. Both methods show meaningful convergence despite stage and structure variation within the peer set.

The two methods triangulate to a median fair value of $6.4B, with a defensible range of $5.1B to $7.8B. The current $15.5B valuation sits materially above this implied range. Key uncertainties include near-term technological de-risking, the extent of any subsequent capital requirements, and market sentiment shifts within the nuclear energy sector. The valuation gap warrants scrutiny of deal dynamics, strategic investor premiums, or material developments not captured in comparable financials.
